newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Canada to push APEC trade, investment agenda.
newsitem.headline: Canada to push APEC trade, investment agenda.

text.p: Canada will work hard to get the 18-member Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum to eliminate barriers to trade and investment in the region, a senior official said on Wednesday.

"We must continue to work forward to lower the barriers to our business people," Leonard Edwards, Canada's assistant deputy minister for trade and economic policy in the Department of Foreign Affairs and International Trade, told reporters.
"Trade investment liberalisation remains a very important part of APEC," he said. "We'll very much be focusing on the implementation part of APEC's work."
He was referring to plans submitted by each country at the leaders' summit in the Philippines last year to foster the growth of trade in the region.

He was also referring to the plan backed by U.S. President Bill Clinton and approved by the summit at Subic Bay to cut tariffs substantially on computers, memory chips and telecommunications equipment beyond the turn of the century.
Edwards, who chairs meetings of APEC's senior officials since Canada was named host of the next summit in Vancouver in November, said one area for progress should be in trade facilitation.

"This is the work on customs procedures and forms, the work on standardisation, the building of databases on rules applying to government procurement and investment regimes. You will find Canada will be pushing pretty hard on trade facilitation," he said.

But Edwards said proposals to cut tariffs further may be difficult to implement because many APEC countries already had low duties and it might be better to seek improvements in opening parts of the economy such as the services sector.

Aside from drafting measures to eliminate trade barriers, Edwards said APEC must get the business community of all 18 member countries more involved in working groups drafting policies for energy, transport and urban development projects.
"We have to give greater emphasis to the role of business in APEC. All (APEC) ministerial meetings in Canada this year will involve significant business events," he said.
APEC will also work on broadening ties with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to expand the level of support for the economic policies being adopted by its members.
"We need to engage more of civil society in what we are doing. I think the fundamental economics are pretty straight forward," he said.

APEC groups Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
